name: Brout-Englert-Gunzig Causal Universe
description: An open universe that begins at one event of empty Minkowski space and fills the forward light cone of that event. A fireball of particle creation expands almost as de Sitter space and then joins smoothly onto a freely expanding Friedmann universe, with no singularity, no event horizon, and no particle horizon.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
To Robert Brout, François Englert, and Edgard Gunzig, the big bang was "more a confession of desperation and bewilderment than the outcome of logical argumentation" [brout1979causal]. At the Université Libre de Bruxelles they proposed a universe that starts at one event of empty flat space and has no singularity [brout1978, brout1979causal]. They wrote the full account by July 1977, published it in Annals of Physics in September 1978, and won the first award of the Gravity Research Foundation that year with the essay "The Causal Universe" [brout1978, brout1979causal, englert1986]. Matter that is created has positive energy. In the cosmological setting the energy of its gravitational field is "exactly equal and opposite", so a universe can fill with matter while its total energy stays that of empty space [brout1979causal]. Edward Tryon had proposed in 1973 that the universe is a fluctuation of the vacuum, a closed one that also conserves energy [tryon1973, smeenk2005].¶Brout, Englert, and Gunzig wrote the cosmological metric as the flat one times a factor, $g_{\mu
u} = (\kappa\phi^2/6)\,\eta_{\mu
u}$, where $\eta_{\mu
u}$ is the Minkowski metric and $\kappa$ the gravitational coupling, and treated $\phi$ as a scalar field in flat space [brout1979causal]. A varying $\phi$ contributes negative energy there, which matter of positive energy balances, and for matter they took a scalar field of mass $m$ [brout1979causal]. A pointlike, isotropic disturbance of $\phi$ at an origin depends on position and time through $	au^2 = t^2 - r^2/c^2$ alone [brout1979causal]. They took space to be empty outside the forward light cone of the origin, with $\phi$ constant there, and let $\phi$ vary inside it [brout1979causal]. The surfaces of constant $	au$ are hyperboloids, so the universe inside the cone is an open one, with spatial curvature $k = -1$ [gott1983, spindel1986]. The mass of the matter field depends on $\phi$ in the flat background, so a changing $\phi$ produces particles, as Leonard Parker had found for quantized fields in an expanding universe, and the particles in turn drive $\phi$ [brout1979causal, parker1969].¶The density of the particles is $n = A\,(mc/\hbar)^3(1+\delta)$, with $A$ of order one and $\delta$ a small correction: particles one Compton wavelength apart [brout1979causal]. The three authors did not treat the first interval, $	au \lesssim \hbar/mc^2$, in which, by the uncertainty principle, the number of particles is not defined [brout1979causal]. With that density as the source, they found "an open universe which closely approximates a de Sitter space" [brout1979causal]. The factor $\phi$ grows without bound at a finite $	au_\infty$, where $\delta$ vanishes and the density of matter is constant: a steady state [brout1979causal]. In proper time $T$ the scale factor of the hyperboloids is close to $a = (c/H)\sinh HT$, with $H = 2/	au_\infty$ [brout1979causal, gott1983, spindel1986]. The pressure of this fireball is negative, close to minus its energy density, and the theorems that predict an initial singularity do not apply to it [brout1979causal, englert1986].¶Creation relies on the quantum coherence of the particles, and it ends once they interact with other fields: near $	au_\infty$ they accelerate apart, radiate, and heat [brout1979causal]. At temperatures of order $mc^2/k_B$ production stops, leaving massive matter and "the ancestor of the present black-body radiation" [brout1979causal]. The universe then expands freely with positive pressure, as in the standard big bang model, and the two stages join smoothly [brout1979causal, gott1983]. The authors did not develop a theory of the transition; they fixed the joining by continuity through two numbers, the present count of baryons and the entropy of radiation per baryon [brout1979causal]. In the worked example of the three authors, with $m = 1$ GeV, creation ends at $	au_1 = 10^{-3}$ s, a proper time of $10^{-2}$ s [brout1979causal]. This universe has no event horizon and no particle horizon: near the origin $a$ grows in proportion to $T$, the conformal time $\int c\,dT/a$ diverges logarithmically there, and any two comoving observers have been in causal contact [brout1979causal, gott1983].¶Brout, Englert, and Philippe Spindel found in 1979 that a self consistent spacetime requires a particle mass of the order of the Planck mass, and interpreted the origin of the universe as a phase transition that breaks a grand unified symmetry [brout1979spindel, brout1980]. With Gunzig, Jean-Marie Frère, Pasquale Nardone, and Claude Truffin they published the full account in 1980: production is a steady state with the geometry of de Sitter space, and it ends when the heavy particles decay [brout1980]. Aharon Casher and Englert took the created objects to be black holes in 1981, and obtained an initial temperature of $4.57	imes10^{16}$ GeV [casher1981]. J. Richard Gott III proposed in 1982 an open universe born at an event of de Sitter space, and wrote that the geometry inside the future light cone of that event is "similar to that found in the Brout, Englert and Spindel (BES) theory" [gott1982]. A year later Gott drew the Penrose diagrams of both: the whole hypersurface on which the Brussels fireball ends is causally connected to the origin, and of the models compared, Gott's alone has an event horizon [gott1983]. Martin Bucher, Alfred Goldhaber, and Neil Turok credited Gott in 1995 with the first proposal of a realistic open universe emerging from de Sitter space, and built a scenario of open inflation on it [bucher1995].¶Gunzig and Nardone showed in 1982 that Minkowski space with a massive quantum scalar field is unstable once $\kappa m^2$ exceeds $288\pi^2$, and likened it to a phase transition between Minkowski and de Sitter space [gunzig1982]. Spindel and P. Vandepeutte integrated the equations numerically in 1986: above the threshold a spatially flat universe that starts empty evolves to de Sitter space with $H = 2/	au_\infty$ [spindel1986]. Instabilities occurred in their integration of the open universes, and they left their conclusions for a later publication [spindel1986].¶Englert wrote in 1986 that the exponential expansion later named inflation had been proposed in the 1978 essay as a solution to the causality problem, and that Alan Guth had proposed a similar solution independently [englert1986, guth1981]. Ilya Prigogine, Jules Géhéniau, Gunzig, and Nardone recast the creation of matter in 1988 as the thermodynamics of an open system, in which spacetime turns into matter and the reverse is forbidden [prigogine1988]. Chris Smeenk, in a 2005 history of inflation, judged that the Brussels programme "led to an increasingly rococo mess", and traced open inflation to Gott's variation on it [smeenk2005]. Robert Brandenberger and Jennie Traschen, writing in 2026, cite the 1978 article among the founding papers of inflation [brandenberger2026].

related.text: The fireball. With the density of created matter constant, the open universe inside the cone is de Sitter space in hyperbolic slices, $a = (c/H)\sinh HT$ [gott1983].
The free expansion. Once creation stops, the universe inside the cone is an open Friedmann one, $k = -1$, with positive pressure [gott1983].
The region outside the forward light cone of the origin, where space is empty and $\phi$ is constant [brout1979causal].
The universe with no creation. At $H = 0$ the fireball's scale factor is $a = cT$, Milne's flat space in hyperbolic slices, and $\phi$ stays constant [brout1979causal, spindel1986].

An open universe inside the light cone of one event, born there by the decay of a false vacuum [coleman1980]. Gott wrote in 1982 that inside the light cone of an event of de Sitter space the geometry is similar to the Brussels one [gott1982].

coordinates.name: Fireball, Flat Background

parameters.description: Flat proper time at which the conformal factor diverges, a positive time. The expansion rate of the fireball is $H = 2/\tau_\infty$
Flat proper time at which creation ends and the free expansion begins, with $0 < \tau_1 < \tau_\infty$
Proper time of the flat background since the origin, along the straight line from the origin through the point. The surfaces of constant $\tau$ are hyperboloids

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \varphi)$ of the flat background about the origin, the event at which the universe starts, and $\tau$ is the flat proper time since that event. The conformal factor is the fireball's with the correction $\delta$ to the density of created particles set to zero [brout1979causal, gott1983]. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Free Expansion, Flat Background

parameters.description: Value the square root of the conformal factor approaches at late times, a pure number. Joining the fireball at $\tau_1$ with the factor and its first derivative continuous fixes $\Omega_f = \left(1 - \tau_1^2/\tau_\infty^2\right)^{-2}$
Flat proper time at which the conformal factor would vanish, before $\tau_1$. The same joining fixes $\tau_b = \tau_1^2/\tau_\infty$
Flat proper time at which the fireball's conformal factor diverges, a positive time
Flat proper time at which creation ends and the free expansion begins, with $0 < \tau_1 < \tau_\infty$
Proper time of the flat background since the origin, along the straight line from the origin through the point. The surfaces of constant $\tau$ are hyperboloids

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \varphi)$ of the flat background about the origin, the event at which the universe starts, and $\tau$ is the flat proper time since that event. The conformal factor is that of the radiation era of the free expansion, an open Friedmann universe with pressure one third of its energy density [gott1983, englert1986]. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Empty Space, Flat Background
domains: r = ct \;\text{with}\; t > 0 \;\text{(the light cone of the origin)}
coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \varphi)$ of the flat background about the origin, the event at which the universe starts. Outside the forward light cone of that event space is empty and the conformal factor is one [brout1979causal]. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Fireball, Proper Time
domains: T = 0 \;\text{(the light cone of the origin)}

parameters.description: Expansion rate of the fireball, $H = 2/\tau_\infty$, an inverse time, with $\tau_\infty$ the flat proper time at which the fireball's conformal factor diverges. The scale factor of the hyperboloids is $a = (c/H)\sinh HT$
Proper time at which creation ends and the free expansion begins, with $\tanh(HT_1/2) = \tau_1/\tau_\infty$ for the flat proper time $\tau_1$ of that moment

coordinates.convention: We use the proper time $T$ of the comoving world lines since the light cone of the origin and the rapidity $\chi$, a pure number, with $t = \tau\cosh\chi$, $r = c\tau\sinh\chi$, and $\tanh(HT/2) = \tau/\tau_\infty$ in the coordinates of the flat background. The scale factor is the fireball's with the correction $\delta$ to the density of created particles set to zero [brout1979causal, gott1983]. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Free Expansion, Proper Time

parameters.description: A time fixed by joining the fireball at $T_1$ with the scale factor and its first derivative continuous, $T_b = T_1 - \sinh(2HT_1)/(2H)$. The scale factor of the hyperboloids is $a = c\sqrt{(T - T_b)^2 - b^2}$
A time fixed by the same joining, $b = \sinh^2(HT_1)/H$
Expansion rate of the fireball, $H = 2/\tau_\infty$, an inverse time, with $\tau_\infty$ the flat proper time at which the fireball's conformal factor diverges
Proper time at which creation ends and the free expansion begins, with $\tanh(HT_1/2) = \tau_1/\tau_\infty$ for the flat proper time $\tau_1$ of that moment

The scale factor is that of the radiation era of the free expansion, an open Friedmann universe with pressure one third of its energy density [gott1983, englert1986]. coordinates.name: Fireball, Conformal Time

parameters.description: Expansion rate of the fireball, $H = 2/\tau_\infty$, an inverse time, with $\tau_\infty$ the flat proper time at which the fireball's conformal factor diverges. The scale factor of the hyperboloids is $a = -c/(H\sinh\eta)$
Conformal time at which creation ends and the free expansion begins, $\eta_1 = \ln(\tau_1/\tau_\infty)$ for the flat proper time $\tau_1$ of that moment, a negative number

coordinates.convention: We use the conformal time $\eta = \ln(\tau/\tau_\infty)$, a pure number with $a\,d\eta = c\,dT$ for the scale factor $a$ and the proper time $T$ of the comoving world lines, and the rapidity $\chi$, with $t = \tau\cosh\chi$ and $r = c\tau\sinh\chi$ in the coordinates of the flat background. The conformal time is itself the chart's $x^0$, and the scale factor is the fireball's with the correction $\delta$ to the density of created particles set to zero [brout1979causal, gott1983]. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Free Expansion, Conformal Time

parameters.description: A time fixed by joining the fireball at $\eta_1$ with the scale factor and its first derivative continuous, $b = 1/(H\sinh^2\eta_1)$. The scale factor of the hyperboloids is $a = bc\sinh(\eta - \eta_b)$
A number fixed by the same joining, $\eta_b = 2\eta_1$
Expansion rate of the fireball, $H = 2/\tau_\infty$, an inverse time, with $\tau_\infty$ the flat proper time at which the fireball's conformal factor diverges

The conformal time is itself the chart's $x^0$, and the scale factor is that of the radiation era of the free expansion [gott1983, englert1986].
